name: Pernambucano Portuguese
notes: Pernambucano (Recife). /t d/ stay stops before [i]: ALiB palatalisation 'é baixa em Aracaju, Maceió, Recife, João Pessoa' (Battisti & Dornelles Filho 2015: 226). Pretonic /e o/ open to [ɛ ɔ] before an open, nasal or low stressed vowel (Mota & Lopes 2018: 215). Coda /S/ is palatal [ʃ ʒ]: 'Comporta-se Recife de forma semelhante ao Rio de Janeiro com o predomínio da pós-alveolar (69,5%)' in NURC (Marins & Margotti 2012: 254); ALiB gives an even split (p. 256). Coda /R/ is the aspirate [h] and is deleted word-finally (Callou, Serra & Cunha 2015: 197, 207).

Mota & Lopes (2018: 215, ALiB, North and Northeast capitals): pretonic mid vowels 'têm uma maior probabilidade de se tornarem médias abertas no contexto de tônica também de timbre aberto (médias-baixas), médias nasais e diante da vogal baixa [a]'; before a close-mid stressed vowel they stay closed in 86 % (/e/) and 91 % (/o/) of tokens. The trigger is the vowel two graphemes to the right, so a pretonic syllable closed by a consonant (espera) keeps the closed vowel.

Callou, Serra & Cunha (2015: 207, ALiB, Northeast capitals): word-final /R/ deletion reaches 94-98 % in verbs and 62-95 % in other words in every capital. Coda /R/ elsewhere is the aspirate [h]: the norm in these capitals is '[- vibrante] e [- anterior]' (p. 197).
The palatal coda sibilant of this variety is [ʃ], so the base rule must also match [ʃ]; the plural endings raise as in the base (dentes, ovos).

The palatal coda /S/ takes the voicing of a following voiced consonant: mesmo [ˈmeʒmu], desde [ˈdeʒdi]. Hora, Henrique & Amorim (2018: 284) cite the palatal variants 'ca[ʃ]ca', 'me[ʒ]mo' e 'doi[ʃ]' as 'estereótipos de falares de outras comunidades linguísticas, como Rio de Janeiro e Recife'. The positional map writes the coda as [ʃ]; this rule voices it in the second pass.
